findings.text: Intel PCI device numbers in this span identify audio controllers per platform plus one volume-management device and one bridge. Assignments include Lakefield audio 0x98c8, Lynx Point LP audio 0x9c20 and 0x9c21, Wellsburg LP 0x9ca0, Skylake LP 0x9d70, Kaby Lake LP 0x9d71, Cannon Lake LP 0x9dc8, Tiger Lake LP 0xa0c8, Skylake 0xa170, Kaby Lake 0xa171, Lewisburg 0xa1f0 and 0xa270, Kaby Lake H 0xa2f0, Cannon Lake H 0xa348, Comet Lake S 0xa3f0, Lunar Lake P 0xa828, NVL 0xd328, Battlemage 0xe2f7, Panther Lake H 0xe328 and Panther Lake 0xe428, Comet Lake R 0xf0c8, Rocket Lake S 0xf1c8, volume management 0x9a0b and bridge 0xb152.

Small-vendor PCI numbers covered are Wangxun vendor 0x8088, ScaleMP vendor 0x8686 with control device 0x1010, Computone vendor 0x8e0e with serial device 0x0302 and subvendor 0x8e0e plus subdevices 0x0001, 0x0002 and 0x0003 for four, eight and six port variants, KTI vendor 0x8e2e with no device shown, Holtek vendor 0x9412 with device 0x6565, and Netmos vendor 0x9710 with device 0x9705.

Adaptec vendor 0x9004 family assigns SCSI-oriented device numbers including 0x6078, 0x1078, 0x8878, 0x2178, 0x3860, 0x5078, 0x5578, 0x6038, 0x6075, 0x6178, 0x7078, 0x7178, 0x7278, 0x7378, 0x7478, 0x7895, 0x8078, 0x8178, 0x8278, 0x8378, 0x8478, 0x8578, 0x8678 and 0x8778 to the 7810 through 7888 generations named in the fragment.

Second Adaptec vendor 0x9005 family assigns device numbers 0x0050, 0x0010, 0x0503, 0x0011, 0x0013, 0x001f, 0x0051, 0x005f, 0x0080, 0x0081, 0x0083, 0x008f, 0x00c0, 0x00c1, 0x00c3, 0x00cf and 0x0500 to the 2940U2, 2930U2, 7890, 3940U2, 3950U2D, 7896, 7892, 7899, Obsidian and Scamp variants named in the fragment.

Netmos serial and multiport device numbers under vendor 0x9710 are 0x9805, 0x9715, 0x9922, 0x9735, 0x9745, 0x9755, 0x9815, 0x9835, 0x9845, 0x9855, 0x9865, 0x9900, 0x9901, 0x9904 and 0x9912, each device number mirroring its model suffix.

Remaining PCI numbers in this span are 3Com variant vendor 0xa727, SolidRun vendor 0xd063, Digium vendor 0xd161 with HFC4S device 0xb410, ExSys subvendor 0xd84d with subdevices 0x4014 and 0x4055, TigerJet vendor 0xe159 with devices 0x0001 and 0x0002, Xilinx RME vendor 0xea60 with audio devices 0x9896, 0x9897 and 0x9898, Xen vendor 0x5853 with platform device 0x0001, plus OCZ vendor 0x1b85 and nCube vendor 0x10ff with no devices shown.
Header is protected against multiple inclusion by a guard macro defined once near the top of the file.
Linux EFI stub interface revision is major value 3 and minor value 0.

Executable identification values are Linux magic 0x818223cd, DOS signature 0x5a4d for letters M Z, NT signature 0x4550 for letters P E followed by two zero bytes, ROM optional-header magic 0x107, 32-bit optional-header magic 0x10b and 64-bit optional-header magic 0x20b.

First group of machine identifiers distinguishes unknown 0x0, host interaction 0x1, Alpha old 0x183, Alpha 0x184, Alpha64 0x284, AM33 0x1d3, AMD64 0x8664, ARM 0x1c0, Thumb 0x1c2, ARMNT 0x1c4, ARM64 0xaa64, ARM64EC 0xa641, ARM64X 0xa64e, CEE 0xc0ee, CEF 0xcef, CHPE x86 0x3a64, byte code 0xebc, i386 0x14c, i860 0x14d, IA64 0x200, LoongArch32 0x6232 and LoongArch64 0x6264, with AXP64 aliasing Alpha64, ARMv7 aliasing ARMNT and hybrid x86 aliasing CHPE x86.

Second group covers M32R 0x9041, M68K 0x268, MIPS16 0x266, MIPS with floating point 0x366, MIPS16 with floating point 0x466, PowerPC 601 0x601, OMNI 0xace1, PA-RISC 0x290, PowerPC 0x1f0, PowerPC with floating point 0x1f1, PowerPC big-endian 0x1f2, R3000 little-endian 0x162 and big-endian 0x160, R4000 0x166, R10000 0x168, RISC-V 32-bit 0x5032, 64-bit 0x5064 and 128-bit 0x5128, SH3 0x1a2, SH3 DSP 0x1a3, SH3E 0x1a4, SH4 0x1a6, SH5 0x1a8, Tahoe 0x7cc, TriCore 0x520 and Windows CE MIPS v2 0x169.

File-header characteristic bits are single-bit flags from 0x1 through 0x8000 marking stripped relocations, executable image, stripped line numbers, stripped local symbols, aggressive working-set trim, large-address awareness, 16-bit machine, low byte-reversed word, 32-bit machine, stripped debug info, run from swap for removable media, run from swap for network images, system file, DLL, uniprocessor-only and high byte-reversed word; the two byte-reversed bits are documented as used together.

Subsystem numbers run from 0 to 17 identifying unknown, native, Windows graphical, Windows console, old Windows CE graphical, OS/2 console, reserved 6, POSIX console, MMOSA, Windows CE graphical, EFI application, EFI boot-service driver, EFI runtime driver, EFI ROM image, Xbox, reserved 15, Windows boot application and Xbox code catalog.

Library and loader feature bits cover lifecycle notifications for process attach 0x1, process detach 0x2, thread attach 0x4 and thread detach 0x8, plus loader traits reserved 0x10, high-entropy address space 0x20, relocatable base 0x40, forced integrity 0x80, execution-prevention compatibility 0x100, no isolation 0x200, no exception handling 0x400, no binding 0x800, thunk or container 0x1000, WDM driver 0x2000, guard control flow 0x4000 and terminal-server awareness 0x8000.

Extended loader characteristics are low-byte bits marking shadow-stack compatibility 0x1, strict enforcement mode 0x2, relaxed context validation 0x4, in-process-only dynamic interfaces 0x8, two reserved bits 0x10 and 0x20, forward-edge integrity annotation 0x40 and hot-patch compatibility 0x80.

Section flags use low bits for index scaling, no-load, grouped, no-pad and copy semantics, content bits for code 0x20, initialized data 0x40 and uninitialized data 0x80, linker bits for other, info, overlay, remove and COMDAT plus reserved 0x2000, then memory-attribute bits from 0x4000 through 0x80000 whose meaning varies by processor family and object versus image use.

Several numeric values are intentionally overloaded so decoding needs context: AXP64 equals Alpha64, ARMv7 equals ARMNT and hybrid x86 equals CHPE x86; thunk and container share 0x1000; protected and no-defer-exception share 0x4000; far-data and pointer-relative share 0x8000; purgeable versus 16-bit and nearby locked and preload bits change meaning between processor families.

PCI vendor, device, subvendor and subdevice numbers are stable 16-bit bus identifiers grouped by vendor blocks; drivers match on vendor plus device and optionally subvendor plus subdevice, so values must not be renumbered.

Signature, machine, characteristic, subsystem and section values describe an on-disk executable format shared with firmware and loaders, so their numeric assignments are fixed interface facts rather than internal enums.
